The drawing shows a pyridine ring, an amide linker, and a diaryl ether, read as follows.

**Pyridine ring:** The ring nitrogen is at the lower left. Moving around the ring from the nitrogen, C2 carries the carboxamide (C=O), C3 carries OH, and C4 carries OMe. C5 and C6 are plain CH, and C6 is bonded to the nitrogen.

**Amide:** C2 is bonded to C(=O)NH, and the NH is attached to a para-substituted benzene ring.

**Diaryl ether:** The para position of that benzene ring carries an O that links to a second phenyl ring. This second ring has an OMe at the meta position relative to the ether oxygen.

Assembled as a SMILES string: COc1ccnc(C(=O)Nc2ccc(Oc3cccc(OC)c3)cc2)c1O

Atom check on the pyridine: c1 (C4, bearing OMe), c (C5), c (C6), n, c (C2, bearing the amide), then c1O (C3, bearing OH), which closes the ring back to C4. This is consistent with the drawing.

SMILES: COc1ccnc(C(=O)Nc2ccc(Oc3cccc(OC)c3)cc2)c1O
